title: Find every subscriber of an event bus, once

blocks.text: The platform team's event bus delivers events to listener methods marked `@Subscribe`. Three bug reports have come in since it went live: the cart-recovery listener never hears about abandoned carts, the onboarding listener's audit trail is empty although its base class subscribes to sign-ups, and the refunds listener, which implements a generic `Listener<E>` interface, receives each refund twice and blows up when a cart event is published.

Registration, delivery and the annotation already work. Finish `subscriberMethods(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/EventBus.java`: given a listener's class, return the methods that should receive events.

When you're done, every method a listener's author marked with `@Subscribe` and gave one parameter receives its events exactly once, whatever its access and whether it is declared in the listener's class or in one of its superclasses. Listeners never override a subscriber method of their superclass. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: each public subscriber of a listener receives the events its parameter type accepts
a method without @Subscribe is not registered, even when its parameter fits
a package-private subscriber method is found and called
a subscriber declared in the listener's superclass is found and called
a subscriber that implements a generic interface method is registered once, so it gets its event once and other events never reach it

origin.section: The Compiler Adds Methods You Never Wrote: Bridges and Lambda Bodies

concepts: A generic override makes javac add a synthetic bridge method taking the erased type, with the method's annotations copied onto it, so a scan that does not skip isBridge() registers the method twice.
getMethods() lists public methods including inherited ones; getDeclaredMethods() lists the class's own methods of every access level and nothing inherited.
Seeing every method of a type whatever its access takes getDeclaredMethods() on the class and on each getSuperclass() until it returns null.
